newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks bounce higher at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks bounce higher at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks powered ahead Tuesday, extending the shy bounce seen at the start of the week on Wall Street's comeback, dealers said.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV jumped 2.5 percent to 706.65, recouping half of last week's losses.
"Prices were boosted by a benign U.S. inflation indicator, which created a good trading environment and sent investors scurrying to cover short positions," said Miguel Daneri at Boston Securities.
However, he warned the U.S. Federal Reserve's actions could not be gauged from a single piece of data.
"Fears of further Fed tightening could return if other indicators show unexpected economic strength," Daneri said.
Technical analysts noted the bolsa had reclaimed the pyschological mark of 700, which could become a support level again if volume continued to improve.

"The market is oversold and wants to go up, especially with the help of the private pension funds which have stepped back in this week and caused turnover to swell," an analyst at a foreign investment bank said. "The question is, will this rise be considered a selling opportunity? If so, we'll know the underlying trend is negative."
Floor volume picked up to a three-week high of 28 million pesos from 20.4 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 81.1 million pesos against 77 million Thursday.
The broad market closed up 1.8 percent, with winners bashing losers 48 to seven and 12 issues closing flat.

Best main-tier performers were steelmakers Siderar and Acindar, which shot up 6.3 percent and 4.1 percent respectively, foods giant Molinos, which surged 4.3 percent, and Bansud bank, up 4.0 percent. The only MerVal loser was real estate developer Irsa, off 0.2 percent.
